Messages.Author: JTP
Messages.Body:
Alright, now with final nights I'm really confused.

It was my understanding that the clan symbols were clan specific, and that
Toreador was not equal to Toreador antitribue (think aire of elation).

But with the introduction of Setite Camarilla members, Ravnos Sabbat,
Assamite Cammies and so forth, what happens to cards that have the
Assamite(or Ravnos, Setite, etc) symbol? Can they only now be used by
Independant Assamites?

If for instance Alamut can affect Tegyrius, Vizier (Cammie Assamite), then
would it now follow that Toreador Antitribue could use aire of elation?

How does consanguinous boon fit into this?

Any help appreciated.

assamite/fos/whatever into a new clan. The toreador and !toreador
should be considered (for all intents and purposes) COMPLETEY
different clans...as if Toreador were known as Toreador and !Toreador

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
JTP wrote:
>
> Alright, now with final nights I'm really confused.
>
> It was my understanding that the clan symbols were clan specific, and that
> Toreador was not equal to Toreador antitribue (think aire of elation).

Correct. Even a Toreador antitribu with a writ of acceptance (making him
a Camarilla Toreador antitribu) could not get +3 bleed with Aire.

> But with the introduction of Setite Camarilla members, Ravnos Sabbat,
> Assamite Cammies and so forth, what happens to cards that have the
> Assamite(or Ravnos, Setite, etc) symbol? Can they only now be used by
> Independant Assamites?

No. They can only be used by Assamites. The card makes no condition on sect.

> If for instance Alamut can affect Tegyrius, Vizier (Cammie Assamite), then

Alamut can be put into play if you control an Assamite. A Camarilla Assamite,
Independent Assamite, and/or a Sabbat Assamite all qualify.

> would it now follow that Toreador Antitribue could use aire of elation?

Can use it, but only for +1/+2, since a Toreador antitribu is not a Toreador.

> How does consanguinous boon fit into this?

It selects clans. Sect is unimportant to Consanguinous Boon.
